sources.title: pLitterStreet paper, section 3.2, printed page 5
sources.finding: Authors ask for discarded rather than functional objects, tight boxes, and a single pile box for inseparable clusters. They describe expert review but acknowledge interpretation differences. Their ten-class taxonomy includes bottles and cups plus a residual other-plastic category. Detailed inclusion rules for cups versus lids, cartons or cans were not found in the reviewed section.

sources.title: Authors' repository README
sources.finding: Describes COCO-format litter annotations and the annotation tool; no detailed cup/bottle decision rules located in the reviewed README.

sources.title: Locally acquired official Zenodo metadata
sources.finding: Dataset description confirms COCO annotations but does not specify cup/bottle inclusion exceptions. Live page timed out; local acquisition metadata was inspected.

project_interpretation: Use original source labels for the existing experiment. Do not treat these broad source guidelines as proof that every ambiguous object is mislabeled. Raw JSON calls the residual category litter; preserve its identifier rather than silently changing the taxonomy.
proposed_review_rule_not_applied: A reviewer should record visible bottle/cup cues, note deformation and visibility, and flag competing interpretations. Relabel only after human adjudication with written class rules. Uncertain material must not be asserted as plastic.
